title: Recovery Verification, Regression Checks & Reliability Learning

content.overview: Repair completion is not proof of restored system performance. Recovery verification repeats the relevant commissioning or operating checks and confirms that corrective action did not create a new failure elsewhere.

vocabulary.definition: A verification that previously functioning related behaviors still work after a change or repair.
Post-correction evidence showing that the affected function again meets defined acceptance criteria.
Return of the same or materially similar failure after corrective action.

sections.title: Repeat the original failed test
sections.body: Use the same or equivalently controlled measurement that demonstrated the fault so before/after evidence is comparable.

sections.title: Check related functions
sections.body: Configuration or equipment changes can affect alarms, neighboring zones, sequencing or data logging. Verify critical related behavior rather than testing only the repaired component.

sections.title: Recurrence reopens the model
sections.body: If the problem returns, review whether the root cause was incomplete, the effectiveness check was too weak or another condition was missed.

workedExamples: After replacing a failed irrigation valve, repeat catch testing and confirm neighboring zone behavior plus alarm/logging state before closing the event.
commonMistakes: Closing when a replacement part is installed.
Testing only the component and not the process outcome.
Ignoring recurrence because the original work order is closed.
content.practicalApplication: Create a recovery-verification checklist for one environmental-control and one irrigation-control repair.
content.summary: Reliability improves when every corrective action is followed by comparable effectiveness evidence and regression checks.
